banner.title: THE DSG DEEPEARTH AREAS 28-29, R547: printed pp. 96-97 (pdf 97-98) - the individual area key descends to the drow and the dark: Area 28 the Realm of the Drow (the vast realm of excavated caverns linking large living caves, the high point of drow culture; the perfectly circular council chamber over a mile in diameter, its dome 1,000 feet from the floor on massive columns, the central vertical shaft to the matriarchs' hall accessible only by flight or levitation; the hundreds of linking caverns and the built cities - buildings erected in the caverns like surface communities; the plentiful water, the huge reservoirs and the placid waterways where boat travel rivals walking; the many levels joined by meticulously sculpted passages and elegant spiral stairways; the miniature council refuges for drow of 4th level or higher where levitation is universal, rope ladders lifting the rest in emergency; the more than 12,000 drow with their rothe and cave pigs; the windpipe's fresh air and the sages' pressure theory; the meticulously clean water, the fungus-farm caverns with their slight surplus, the strict population control; the mines of iron, copper, silver, gold, adamantite and mithril; and the city architecture - soaring columns, buttresses and huge domes lit by phosphorescent fungi, stone buildings with gold and silver ornament never structural), and Area 29 the Dark Realms (the spiderweb of living caves all leading down to the huge central chamber; the trickle that never floats a kayak, the water met as thick cold mud; the chamber with no less than 12 mouth passages each trickling mud into the monstrous reservoir - 300 feet deep, nearly a mile across, its level constant for centuries; the cloakers driven into a few dozen caverns, the mind flayers' evil third of the region, the well-defended derro communities; the unclaimed dark domains of slimes, oozes, jellies, animated fungi and scavengers; the hundred-plus Plane of Earth denizens - earth elementals, xorn, crysmal, galeb duhr, chaggrin, dao - clustered near their escape vortex; the stale foul-smelling air; the nearly unexploited gems and precious metals guarded by deadly hazards; and the mud whirlpool - the slow-motion elemental vortex to the Plane of Earth, its journey the Area 21 procedure without heat damage but with breath held).
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR (djvu.txt lines ~12362-12554) with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (capture idx 216 tail = the Area 28 head, idx 220 = the printed p. 97 window carrying the Area 28 tail and the Area 29 head, idx 225 head = the Area 29 tail); the compiled-tables appendix has no reprint of this prose. A CLEAN-READ ROUND: both machine reads agree on every load-bearing number - the mile diameter, the 1,000-ft dome, the 4th-level refuge gate, the 12,000 drow, the 12 mouth passages, the 300-ft mud depth and mile width, the hundred-plus earth denizens and the illithid third; the only garbles settled cross-read (the djvu Cyrillic-The and /evitation for the capture The and levitation). SEAMS: the R518 water travel (the drow waterways and boat travel), the Monster Manual denizens (the drow, rothe, cave pigs, cloakers, mind flayers, derro, xorn, crysmal, galeb duhr, chaggrin, dao and the oozes), the PHB levitate/fly and the Area 21 vortex procedure, and the R521-R522 mining (the drow mines and the unexploited veins). A ZERO-FLIP ROUND: the pp. 75-98 Deepearth child remains open until the setting lands in full (the R527/R533-R546 precedent - the gap report is NOT in the git add). Nothing auto-credits.
banner.sentinel: A procedural-plus-prose round: no tables pin. The numbers pin as consts per the R508 convention - the dome height, the refuge level, the drow population, the mouth-passage count, the mud depth and the earth-denizen count, with the mile diameters and the illithid third pinned as bools of prose. The geography, denizens, resources and unique-features prose pins as bools for both areas; no dice appear in this round. The water-travel/MM/PHB/mining seams are noted; the Deepearth child stays open; nothing auto-credits.

consts.name: dnapDomeHtFt
consts.comment: the council chamber ceiling rises to a dome 1,000 feet from the floor.

consts.name: dnapRefugeLvl
consts.comment: the miniature council refuges admit only drow of 4th level or higher.

consts.name: dnapMouthPassages
consts.comment: the central chamber has access to no less than 12 connecting passages, each carrying a slow trickle of mud.

consts.name: dnapMudDeepFt
consts.comment: the mud reservoir measures some 300 feet deep.

consts.name: dnapEarthDenizens
consts.comment: a hundred or more denizens of the Plane of Earth cluster near the center of the Dark Realms, where their escape route is always near.

bools.name: dnapExcavatedRealm
bools.comment: this vast realm contains many excavated caverns linking a number of large living caves, and is the high point of drow culture in Deepearth.

bools.name: dnapCouncilChamber
bools.comment: central to the drow realm is a perfectly circular chamber laboriously hollowed out from the rock, its ceiling rising to a dome supported by many massive columns, with a vertical shaft through the center leading to the matriarchs' council hall.

bools.name: dnapMileDiameter
bools.comment: the circular council chamber is over a mile in diameter.

bools.name: dnapFlightOnlyShaft
bools.comment: the matriarchs' council shaft is accessible only by flight or levitation.

bools.name: dnapBuiltCities
bools.comment: drow dwellings fill the hundreds of linking caverns; unlike the duergar or svirfneblin, the drow erect buildings in the caverns - communities that would resemble surface dwellers' but for the encompassing darkness and looming ceilings.

bools.name: dnapWaterways
bools.comment: water flows plentifully and the drow have created huge reservoirs; wide placid waterways connect many caverns, and boat travel is nearly as common as walking.

bools.name: dnapSculptedPassages
bools.comment: the realm includes caverns on many different levels, but all connecting passages have been meticulously sculpted, with elegant spiral stairways circling shafts in the rock.

bools.name: dnapMiniRefuges
bools.comment: occasionally miniature versions of the matriarchs' council chamber allow access only to drow of 4th level or higher, since that is the level at which levitation ability becomes universal; in dire emergency rope ladders lift the rest of the population into these refuges, virtually impervious to attack.

bools.name: dnapMastery
bools.comment: the drow leave no doubt as to their complete mastery of their realm.

bools.name: dnapRothePigs
bools.comment: the drow raise rothe and cave pigs for food and wool; a few rats and bats also dwell here, but other monsters are as rare as in the streets of a bustling surface city.

bools.name: dnapWindpipeAir
bools.comment: the bottom access tunnel to the windpipe provides a steady flow of fresh air; the drow do not understand the cause, but their sages postulate that small crust fluctuations cause great air-pressure changes in the narrow shaft.

bools.name: dnapCleanWater
bools.comment: water is abundant and the drow keep their water sources clean with meticulous dedication.

bools.name: dnapFungusFarms
bools.comment: many large caverns are devoted exclusively to fungus growing, a food supply capable of feeding the populace with a slight surplus; population is strictly controlled, with imperfect babies ruthlessly killed at birth.

bools.name: dnapDrowMines
bools.comment: the drow work a series of mines supplying their complex metalworking: iron, copper, silver, gold, and occasional finds of adamantite and mithril.

bools.name: dnapCityArchitecture
bools.comment: the drow cities are marvels of subterranean architecture - soaring columns, elegant buttresses and huge domes; despising sunlight, they employ numerous phosphorescent fungi among their dwellings to display the architecture.

bools.name: dnapStoneOrnament
bools.comment: all buildings consist primarily of expertly sculpted stone for smooth lines and a clean look; prominent offices or wealthy dwellings are embellished with gold and silver ornamentations, never structurally essential, only to enhance appearance.

bools.name: dnapSpiderwebCaves
bools.comment: this is a region of living caves; a map would resemble a spiderweb, with all the peripheral caves leading down toward a huge central cavern.

bools.name: dnapMudNotWater
bools.comment: enough water trickles through to add lustre to the formations but never gathers volume enough to float even a kayak; the water is generally encountered as thick, cold mud.

bools.name: dnapMudReservoir
bools.comment: the chamber contains a monstrous reservoir of thick mud; though mud continually flows in, the level has remained constant for centuries.

bools.name: dnapMudMileAcross
bools.comment: the mud reservoir is nearly a mile across.

bools.name: dnapCloakerRemnant
bools.comment: the alien culture of the cloakers, once prolific throughout Deepearth, has been driven into a narrow region of a few dozen caverns.

bools.name: dnapIllithidThird
bools.comment: the mind flayers hold more territory - roughly a third of this entire region falls under their evil dominion.

bools.name: dnapDerroRedoubts
bools.comment: several small communities of derro hold sway over localized caverns that are always well defended.

bools.name: dnapDarkDomains
bools.comment: virtually every creature of darkness is represented; the many caverns unclaimed by intelligent races are the domains of slimes, oozes, jellies, animated fungi, scavengers and all the other unintelligent creatures that prowl the Underdark in search of prey.

bools.name: dnapEarthRoster
bools.comment: earth elementals are the most numerous of the cluster, but xorn, crysmal, galeb duhr, chaggrin and dao may also be encountered; the earth creatures unite to defend against any threat to the vortex leading to their plane.

bools.name: dnapStaleAir
bools.comment: the air in the Dark Realms is generally stale and foul-smelling; the water supply is sufficient to keep the air humid and provide drinking water for creatures not particular about quality, but could not support a community of more humanoid inhabitants.

bools.name: dnapUnminedWealth
bools.comment: there is a great deal of mineral wealth here, nearly all of it unexploited; the areas around the vortex have been thoroughly scavenged by the Plane of Earth creatures (particularly the crysmal), but the rest offers a wide variety of gems and precious metals for the intrepid miner - the deadly hazards forestall almost any mining operation, however.

bools.name: dnapMudWhirlpool
bools.comment: a creature flying over the center of the mud lake can see the mud spinning deliberately, like a watery whirlpool in slow motion: an elemental vortex to the Plane of Earth, very similar to the Area 21 Plane of Fire connection, with mud seeping through at just the pace matching the inflow.

bools.name: dnapEarthJourney
bools.comment: moving from the Prime Plane to the Plane of Earth requires the same procedure as the Area 21 journey to the Plane of Fire; travelers take no heat damage but must hold their breath or carry breathable air for the time spent in transit.

examples.note: the chamber and the refuges: the 1,000-ft dome, the 4th-level levitation gate.
the mud chamber: 12 mouth passages, the 300-ft-deep reservoir.
the earth cluster: a hundred or more denizens near the vortex.
